## Proof

Let $(U, \phi)$ be a smooth chart on $M$ with $\phi: U \to \widehat{U} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ a diffeomorphism. The component functions are $x^i: U \to \mathbb{R}$, so by definition of the chart,

$$\phi = (x^1, \dots, x^n), \qquad \phi(q) = \big(x^1(q), \dots, x^n(q)\big) \in \mathbb{R}^n.$$

**Coordinate representation.** For any smooth function $f: U \to \mathbb{R}$, its coordinate representation (push-forward) under the chart $\phi$ is the function on $\widehat{U}$ defined by

$$\widehat{f} := f \circ \phi^{-1}: \widehat{U} \to \mathbb{R}.$$

Applying this to $f = x^j$:

$$\widehat{x^j} = x^j \circ \phi^{-1}: \widehat{U} \to \mathbb{R}.$$

**Evaluation in coordinates.** Let $(a^1, \dots, a^n) \in \widehat{U}$. Since $\phi$ is a diffeomorphism, there is a unique $q \in U$ with $\phi(q) = (a^1, \dots, a^n)$, i.e. $\phi^{-1}(a^1, \dots, a^n) = q$. By the definition of $\phi$ as the tuple of component functions,

$$\phi(q) = (a^1, \dots, a^n) \iff x^i(q) = a^i \text{ for all } i = 1, \dots, n.$$

Therefore

$$\widehat{x^j}(a^1, \dots, a^n) = x^j\!\big(\phi^{-1}(a^1, \dots, a^n)\big) = x^j(q) = a^j.$$

**Conclusion.** The coordinate representation of $x^j$ is the $j$-th coordinate projection on $\widehat{U}$:

$$\boxed{\widehat{x^j} = x^j \circ \phi^{-1}, \qquad \widehat{x^j}(a^1, \dots, a^n) = a^j.}$$

In other words, under the chart $\phi$, the component function $x^j$ on $M$ becomes exactly the $j$-th standard coordinate function on the open set $\widehat{U} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$. The coordinates $(a^1, \dots, a^n)$ of a point $\phi(q) \in \widehat{U}$ are precisely the values of the component functions at $q$: $a^i = x^i(q)$. This is the sense in which the chart "identifies" the abstract coordinate functions $x^i$ on $M$ with the canonical Cartesian coordinate functions on $\mathbb{R}^n$.

### PROOF COMPLETE
